channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Wildberries Expands Central Asian Operations with New Distribution Hubs
item.description: Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries is establishing new distribution centers in Central Asia to mitigate disruptions from Ukrainian drone attacks. Agreements have been signed to build a $140 million complex near Tashkent, Uzbekistan, creating 7,500 jobs. Warehouses are also planned near Almaty and Astana, Kazakhstan, expected to be operational by 2027. These facilities will serve both local and Russian markets.

item.title: Construction Begins on Europe's Largest Green Hydrogen Project
item.description: Moeve has started construction on the first phase of the Andalusian Green Hydrogen Valley in Palos de la Frontera, Spain. The project, described as Europe's largest in its segment, will initially feature 300 MW of electrolyzers with potential for expansion. Investments exceed 1 billion euros, and the project is expected to create over 8,000 jobs and support local businesses.

item.title: Kazakhstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Reviews Major Infrastructure Projects in Almaty
item.description: First Deputy Prime Minister Nurlan Nalbaye reviewed the progress of major infrastructure, social, and utility projects in Almaty city and region. The review included plans for developing Almaty International Airport, expanding the Almaty-Taldykorgan and Almaty-Bishkek highways, and modernizing the City Clinical Hospital No. 7 to a 900-bed capacity.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Set Water Intake Limits for Amu Darya and Syr Darya Rivers for 2026-2027
item.description: Central Asian countries have approved water intake limits and reviewed reservoir operating modes for the Amu Darya and Syr Darya river basins for the 2026-2027 inter-vegetation period. The decision was made at the 95th meeting of the Interstate Coordination Water Commission (ICWC) in Turkmenbashi. The Shardara reservoir in Kazakhstan received more water than expected.

item.title: US Secretary of State Visits Athens, Urges Europe to Increase Defense Responsibility
item.description: During a visit to Athens for the 6th round of the Greek-US Strategic Dialogue, Secretary of State Antony Blinken emphasized the need for Europe to take greater responsibility for its own defense amidst evolving security and energy landscapes. Discussions covered defense, security, energy, technology, trade, and investment, highlighting Greece's role as a key US partner in regional security and energy planning.

item.title: UN: Taliban detained over 50 women for dress code violations in three months
item.description: The UN mission reported that Taliban authorities detained at least 52 women and one girl in Kabul and Herat over a three-month period for alleged dress code violations. These included visible hair and wearing colorful scarves or makeup. The UN warned that the actual number of detentions could be higher due to reporting concerns.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Jordan to Enhance Parliamentary Oversight of Agreements
item.description: Uzbekistan and Jordan are set to strengthen parliamentary oversight of agreements. During the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly, Uzbekistan's Senate Chairperson met with Jordan's House of Representatives First Deputy Speaker. Both sides emphasized the importance of implementing agreements, particularly those related to trade, economy, education, and tourism, to boost bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Georgia to Actively Continue Positive Cooperation Trends
item.description: Uzbekistan and Georgia will actively continue positive cooperation trends. During the 153rd IPU Assembly, Uzbekistan's Senate Chairperson met with Georgia's Parliament Speaker. They highlighted the strong foundation for bilateral relations and potential for expanded cooperation in trade, investment, transport, and culture. A joint roadmap for inter-parliamentary cooperation was proposed.

item.title: Robust Human Rights Protection is Foundation for Justice and Lasting Peace
item.description: Discussions at the 153rd IPU Assembly focused on the role of parliaments in upholding international humanitarian law and human rights. Participants emphasized strengthening national legislation, accountability mechanisms, and protecting human dignity, especially in conflict zones. Uzbekistan's Senate Chairperson highlighted the shared goal of protecting life and dignity in all circumstances.

item.title: Regions with the highest urban population in Kazakhstan named
item.description: Kazakhstan's urban population has reached 64.2%, an increase of 5.2 percentage points in six years, according to the National Statistics Bureau. The regions with the highest urban population share are Karaganda (82.8%), Ulytau (79.7%), Aktobe (76.7%), Pavlodar (71.7%), and East Kazakhstan (67.9%). Experts note rapid urban growth in 2024-2026.

item.title: Uzbek President proposes accelerating alliance for critical minerals in Central Asia
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed accelerating the formation of an alliance for critical minerals among Central Asian countries. He highlighted the region's significant raw material reserves vital for modern industry and new technologies. Mirziyoyev suggested a unified digital map of critical mineral reserves as a first step.

item.title: Taliban report seizure of over 600 kg of opium from an ambulance in Takhar
item.description: Taliban security forces in Takhar province reported the seizure of 614 kilograms of opium from a private ambulance originating from Badakhshan. This is the second such discovery in Takhar within a month. The report comes amid Taliban claims of zero poppy cultivation, though UN confirms reduced cultivation but existing stockpiles.

item.title: Central Asian leaders discuss transport and logistics network development
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized the need to connect Central Asian countries with a modern transport and logistics network. Speaking at a summit, he stated that the region can become a major hub for global trade and economic activity. Mirziyoyev called for coordinated development of transport infrastructure to create a unified system and attract investment.

item.title: Online Academy Offers Education to Afghan Girls Barred from School
item.description: The Behdukht Online Academy provides free education to Afghan girls who are banned from attending school. Founded in 2023, the volunteer-run initiative addresses the crisis of 2.4 million girls being deprived of secondary education. The situation has also impacted female teachers, with numbers decreasing and salaries dropping significantly.

item.title: Indian Court Orders Release of Tanker Crew, Including Kazakh National
item.description: An Indian court has ordered the repatriation of 23 sailors, including a Kazakh national, from the arrested tanker Unity. The crew had been abandoned by the shipowner, facing unpaid wages and shortages of supplies. The court directed authorities to arrange their return within three weeks and recover costs from the responsible parties.

item.title: Uzbek President Calls for Flexible Cooperation Format Among Central Asian States
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that Central Asian nations do not seek to build large, complex structures but rather a flexible format for cooperation. He emphasized mutual respect, trust, and pragmatism among sovereign states. Mirziyoyev noted that this approach has already yielded results, increasing the region's visibility and interest from international partners.

item.title: Indian Court Orders Repatriation of Crew from Tanker Unity, Including Kazakh National
item.description: An Indian court has ordered the repatriation of the crew from the detained tanker Unity, which has been anchored in Paradip port since May due to a commercial dispute. The court recognized the sailors as abandoned by the shipowner and mandated swift action, potentially within three weeks, with costs recoverable from the owner. A Kazakh national is among the crew.

item.title: Central Asian and Azerbaijani Leaders Convene in Turkmenistan for Consultative Meeting
item.description: Leaders from Central Asia and Azerbaijan met in Turkmenistan's Avaza National Tourist Zone on October 8, 2026. The meeting, attended by heads of state from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan, focused on enhancing political, economic, and cultural cooperation. Participants discussed joint initiatives and adopted decisions on regulatory documents and a joint statement.

item.title: UNICEF Expands Primary Healthcare for Mothers and Children in Afghanistan with Korean Support
item.description: UNICEF is strengthening primary healthcare services and expanding access for mothers and children in Afghanistan, supported by Korea. The organization announced on X that its programs include vaccination and nutrition services, emphasizing every child's right to good health. This initiative addresses the lack of quality healthcare in remote Afghan areas.

item.title: Air Arabia Considers New Flights to Uzbekistan's Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva
item.description: Air Arabia is considering launching new flight routes to the Uzbek cities of Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva. The airline also discussed increasing the number of flights from Tashkent to Sharjah and Abu Dhabi. Currently, 13 weekly flights operate on these routes.

item.title: Taliban Official: Helicopter Damaged by Rocks During Landing in Panjshir
item.description: A Taliban official in Panjshir stated a helicopter was slightly damaged by rocks during an unsuitable landing, denying claims of it being shot down. The 'Green Trend' group alleged they downed a helicopter carrying a Taliban Air Force chief. Local sources confirmed a low-flying helicopter but could not access the mountainous area.

item.title: Almaty Assigns Heating Season Responsibilities Across All Eight Districts
item.description: Almaty is commencing its 2026-2027 heating season on October 9th, with a phased rollout starting with socially significant facilities. Designated specialists in each of the city's eight districts will be available to address resident inquiries regarding heating connections and issues. A 24/7 operational response team will also be active.

item.title: US President Trump: Constructive Talks Underway with Iran, No New Attacks Planned
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated that constructive talks are ongoing with Iran and ruled out new US attacks before the November midterm elections. He noted record oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, emphasizing that no oil entered or left Iran during a recent 24-hour period.

item.title: Afghanistan's UN Envoy Urges End to Arbitrary Detentions and Torture
item.description: Afghanistan's acting UN representative, Naseer Ahmad Faiq, called for an end to arbitrary detentions, torture, killings, and forced disappearances in Afghanistan. He urged support for an independent investigative mechanism and the criminalization of gender apartheid. Faiq also stressed that Afghan asylum seekers should not be returned to dangerous areas and humanitarian aid must be provided without discrimination.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Foreign Ties Through New Projects and Political Dialogue
item.description: Kazakh diplomats held meetings with international partners to discuss expanding investment, trade, economic, and political cooperation. Discussions included new joint projects, particularly with Japan in digital infrastructure, critical minerals, transport, and agriculture. Kazakhstan also explored trade and investment growth with Greece, which has nearly 50 businesses operating in the country.

item.title: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov Inspects Progress on Modernizing Balkhash City's Infrastructure
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov visited Balkhash city in the Karaganda region to review the implementation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directives on socio-economic development. The region, a major industrial center, is diversifying its economy beyond mining and metallurgy. Significant funds are allocated for social development, including education, culture, sports, social security, and healthcare.

item.title: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov Reviews System-Forming Enterprises in Balkhash City
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov visited Balkhash city to familiarize himself with the operations of its key enterprises, the modernization of mining and metallurgy complexes, plans for new industrial facilities, and geological exploration results. The Karaganda region's industrial output increased by 4.7% in January-August, with manufacturing ranking second in Kazakhstan. Modern exploration technologies were presented.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Consulate in Bangkok Warns of Issues with Thai E-Visa Website
item.description: Uzbekistan's Consulate General in Bangkok has alerted citizens to disruptions on the official Thai E-Visa website. This announcement follows complaints about visa acquisition difficulties. Travelers reported delays in visa confirmation, with some receiving approval but not the visa file via email. The Consulate advises planning travel considering potential technical issues and applying for e-visas in advance.

item.title: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov Inspects Infrastructure Projects in Balkhash
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov visited Balkhash to review infrastructure modernization, including the Balkhash Thermal Power Plant, a new angiography center at a multidisciplinary hospital, and the Balkhash industrial zone. The new medical center, funded by returned state assets, provides 24/7 emergency vascular care. The project enhances access to specialized medical services for approximately 150,000 residents in the region.

item.title: Prosecutor's office investigates woman's critical condition post-childbirth in Tashkent
item.description: The prosecutor's office is investigating the case of a woman in Tashkent who has been in critical condition for six months after childbirth. The Health Department stated that the medical care provided to the patient followed clinical protocols. A forensic medical examination has been ordered.

item.title: Kazakhstan to increase supply of AI-92 gasoline and diesel fuel in October
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to supply 1.239 million tons of fuel to the domestic market in October, exceeding September's plan. Supplies of AI-92 gasoline will increase to 442,283 tons, and diesel fuel to 610,172 tons. Exports of gasoline and diesel fuel are also planned.

item.title: One of three missing Kazakh citizens in Nepal and Tibet found safe
item.description: One of three Kazakh women who went missing in Nepal and Tibet following natural disasters has been found safe in Kazakhstan. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed contact with her and stated she did not travel to the disaster zone. Efforts continue to locate the other two missing citizens.

item.title: Turkmenistan prioritizes TAPI pipeline and Caspian Sea route for gas exports
item.description: Turkmenistan is accelerating efforts to diversify its natural gas exports. The first section of the TAPI pipeline to Herat is expected by end-2026. The trans-Caspian pipeline is now a priority, as China currently takes most Turkmen gas. Turkmenistan signed a letter of intent for gas distribution in Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Vice President Karine Orders Enhanced Efforts for Interethnic Harmony
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karine chaired a meeting on strengthening interethnic harmony and implementing presidential directives. He instructed state bodies to improve interaction mechanisms and continue informational work on presidential theses. Karine emphasized the importance of constitutional values, rule of law, and national unity, stating that discrimination is prohibited and attempts to undermine unity will be suppressed.

item.title: Strengthening Interethnic Accord Discussed at Kazakhstan's Akorda
item.description: Kazakhstan's Akorda hosted a meeting chaired by Vice-President Yerlan Karin to discuss strengthening interethnic harmony and implementing President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directives from the first session of the People's Council. Participants included heads of key ministries and the General Prosecutor's Office. The meeting emphasized the importance of constitutional values of interethnic and interfaith accord as a foundation for the nation's stable development.

item.title: Uzbekistan Imposes New Entry Requirements for Travelers to Egypt
item.description: Starting November 1, Uzbekistan citizens will need to obtain entry visas for Egypt in advance from Egyptian diplomatic missions. Tourist trips must be organized through authorized tour operators. Travelers under 40 require pre-approved visas and must be accompanied by close family members, with a minimum of $5,000 in cash. Independent travelers over 40 need at least $3,000.

item.title: Almaty City Administration Addresses Concerns Over Hazardous Wheelchair Ramps
item.description: The Almaty city administration has responded to resident complaints about hazardous wheelchair ramps in the reconstructed Republic Square. Some ramps are reportedly damaged, and their usability for people with limited mobility is questioned, with one user noting stairs at the end of a ramp. The administration acknowledges the issue and plans to repair and improve the ramps as part of ongoing landscaping work.

item.title: Afghanistan's UN Representative Urges Taliban to End Gender Apartheid
item.description: Naseer Ahmad Faiq, Afghanistan's acting UN representative, called on the Taliban to end gender apartheid and discriminatory decrees against women and girls. He stated that these policies contradict Islamic teachings and Afghan culture, depriving women and girls of basic rights and opportunities.

item.title: Business Manager of Karachaganak Support Service Sentenced to 10 Years for Embezzling $2.2 Million
item.description: A court in Uralsk has sentenced Barlyk Mendygaziyev, business manager of Karachaganak Support Service (KSS), to 10 years in prison for embezzling $2.2 million. He defrauded the company by transferring funds to a US-based firm he controlled under the guise of purchasing equipment.

item.title: Russian religious figure opposing Ukraine war sentenced to 4 years in Almaty
item.description: A religious figure from Russia, known for opposing the war in Ukraine, has been sentenced to four years in prison in Almaty. Additionally, an investigation reveals the son-in-law of the President of Uzbekistan has secretly obtained UAE citizenship. A Dutch company developed software for easy control of multiple drones from one system.
